deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a category C with weak equivalences W and cofibrations Cof, i.e. a left-sided ('cofibration category' / 'catégorie à cofibrations') structure in the sense of a dual of K. Brown's categories of fibrant objects. C_cof is the full subcategory of cofibrant objects. Pushouts are only assumed to exist along cofibrations.

Step 3° studies the comparison functor Psi: W_cof^{-1} C_cof -> W^{-1} C between the two localizations.

Proposition. Psi is an equivalence of categories iff condition (*) holds:
(*) For every diagram x ⇉ y -> y', with two parallel maps phi, psi: x -> y and f: y -> y' in W, such that f∘phi = f∘psi and x, y cofibrant, one has [phi] = [psi] in W_cof^{-1} C_cof.
- The objects x, y lie in C_cof; y' is arbitrary.
- One automatically has [phi] = [psi] in W^{-1}C, since f becomes invertible there.
- Hence (*) is implied by Psi being faithful, which gives necessity.
- Essential surjectivity and fullness are presumably supplied by cofibrant replacement and factorization axioms established earlier. So (*) is the only obstruction, namely to faithfulness.

Grothendieck then decides to work inside C_cof, i.e. to assume every object is cofibrant. In a bracketed NB he records that C_cof with the induced W and Cof is again a structure of the same type (axiom 'C3' still holds). He also notes that the inclusion C_cof -> C preserves the only pushouts whose existence is postulated: squares a <- ... with f or g a cofibration.

He then defines, for objects x, y, a category Ch_0(x,y) whose objects are cospans x --f--> · <--i-- y with i in W ∩ Cof (a trivial cofibration); morphisms are commutative maps of such diagrams. 'Ch' plausibly stands for 'chemins'.

Composition Ch_0(x,y) × Ch_0(y,z) -> Ch_0(x,z), (F,G) ↦ G∘F, is defined by pushout:
- Start from (f,i) for x and (g,j) for y.
- Push out g along the trivial cofibration i. This gives g' and a map that is again a trivial cofibration, since trivial cofibrations are stable under cobase change.
- The composite is (g'∘f, k∘j)-type data, with k the cobase change of i.

This is the standard way of building a 'mapping category' of left fractions. The aim is that pi_0 Ch_0(x,y), or its nerve, computes Hom_{W^{-1}C}(x,y), or the mapping space. These composites are associative only up to coherent isomorphism, i.e. they form a bicategory-type structure. The page breaks off at the composition formula.
errors: The parenthetical '(donc [phi]=[psi] dans W^{-1}C)' is trivially true since f is inverted in W^{-1}C. It is the reason (*) is necessary, not a consequence needing proof.

Sufficiency of (*) is asserted without proof on this page; it relies on unstated earlier axioms (cofibrant replacement, factorization). In standard cofibration categories (Brown, Cisinski) Psi is always an equivalence, so (*) would be automatic there. The proposition is meaningful only for Grothendieck's weaker axiom set.

Pushout-composition of cospans is associative only up to canonical isomorphism, so the 'accouplements' define a bicategory/pseudo-structure rather than a strict composition. This is not addressed on the page.

ideas.what: Comparison W_cof^{-1}C_cof -> W^{-1}C is an equivalence iff a faithfulness condition holds
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy category of a cofibration category computed on cofibrant objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: K. S. Brown (1973, dual form); Quillen (1967) for model categories; Cisinski 'Catégories dérivables' (2010); Rădulescu-Banu
ideas.where_published: Possibly related discussions in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs; not identified precisely

ideas.what: Restriction to cofibrant objects gives again a cofibration-type structure, with the inclusion preserving the postulated pushouts
ideas.modern_name: Full subcategory of cofibrant objects of a cofibration category

ideas.what: Category Ch_0(x,y) of cospans x -> · <- y with trivial-cofibration backward leg, composed by pushout
ideas.modern_name: Cospan / left-fraction mapping categories; hammock localization restricted to length-2 zigzags; Weiss's hammocks in Waldhausen categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dwyer–Kan (1980); Weiss (1999); Cisinski (2010); Bénabou-style bicategory of cospans

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard development of the homotopy theory of cofibration categories: cofibrant restriction, faithfulness criterion, and cospan mapping categories composed by pushout. All of it is in Brown, Dwyer–Kan, Waldhausen, Weiss and Cisinski. It is historically interesting as a 1982 Grothendieck precursor to Pursuing Stacks/Dérivateurs, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'il f. et s.' = 'il faut et il suffit'.
'les relations [?] de C_cof dans C' is more likely 'l'inclusion de C_cof dans C commute aux sommes amalgamées voulues'.
'une catégorie [?] : C3' is likely 'une catégorie à cofibrations (vérifiant C3)', i.e. it satisfies the same axioms.
In the Ch_0 definition, the crossed-out text is an earlier 'où ... ∈ W∩cof', replaced by 'où i ∈ W ∩ cof'.
The composition formula at the bottom reads roughly '(g,j)∘(f,i) = (g'f, k j)', with k the cobase change of i along g.
